WEEK 1 RESOURCES AND DECISION MAKING ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS: By the end of the lesson, students should be able to ➢ Discuss the following; family needs and resources ➢ Highlight the two different types of needs with an example each. ➢ Differentiate between needs and wants ➢ Outline the characteristics of

FAMILY NEEDS Needs are things that are essential. The family members have physical, emotional, mental and social needs. Wants are those things you desire though they are not essential for your health and well-being. TYPES OF FAMILY NEEDS 1. Basic or primary needs are very important needs which the family cannot do without. They include: ▪ Food ▪ Housing ▪ Clothing ▪ Health care 2. Secondary needs are those things the family wants that are not as important as the primary needs. The family can do without them. They include: ▪ Recreation ▪ Pocket money ▪ Extra clothing ▪ Family car etc. FAMILY RESOURCES Resources are those things which the families can use to meet their needs and reach their goals. CLASSIFICATION OF FAMILY RESOURCES

1. Human resources: These are resources which exist within an individual. They are personal to each individual. They include: a. Knowledge: This includes everything a person has observed, learned and remembers. E.g. How to launder the family clothes. b. Skills: These are a special set of abilities that allow a person to perform certain tasks well. E.g. drawing, sewing and baking etc. c. Imagination: This is the ability of the mind to be creative and resourceful. d. Energy: This is the power that helps you get things done. Energy is used to do work. e. Time: Time is used with other resources to reach goals. 2. Material or non-human resources: these are resources that exist outside people but can be controlled owned or used by the family. Types of material resources: a. Possessions: These are the things the family owns, which they can use to attain some goals. Family possession could be: ▪ Those possessions that last a long time and are not used up readily. They are durable. E.g. are furniture, car, houses and appliances. ▪ Those possessions that are used up quickly e.g. food, clothes, paper etc. b. Money: Money is used to measure the value of the goods we have. Other resources the family can use ▪ Community resources: every community has facilities, institutions and organizations. These organizations help families to: ❖ Improve their skills ❖ Solve their problems ❖ Enjoy life ▪ Natural resources: these are air, water, land, plants, animals and minerals. These are found in our surroundings or environment. CHARACTERISTICS OF RESOURCES

1. Utility: This means that resources have value and worth and that they can be applied for producing goods and services. 2. Accessibility: This means that resources must exist on hand or in reserve for goal attainment. 3. Inter-changeability: A resource is interchangeable when it can be substituted with another resource to reach goals. 4. Manageability: All resources are to some degree manageable. This means that they can be controlled for the purpose of achieving goals. REVIEW QUESTIONS 1. Explain the term “family needs”. 2. Outline the two types of needs giving three examples each. 3. Discuss two classifications of family resources. 4. Outline any three characteristics of resources. 5. .......... Are used for meeting family needs. (a) goals (b) resources (c) standard (d) tools. 6. Human resources exist in (a) books (b) individuals (c) classes (d) school. 7. Decision making occurs when there ....... to choose from. (a)is an object (b) is one action (c)up to one situation (d)are more than one situation. 8. Which of the following is not a human resource? (a) money (b) skill (c) knowledge (d) energy. 9. Decisions can easily be influenced by (a) resources (b) period (c) time (d)self. 10.The process of choosing are alternatives is called (a) actions (b) action making (c) decision making (d) alternating. Nutrition is the scientific study of food. Food is any substance which, when eaten is able to build the body, provide heat and energy or regulate body processes. The quality and value of any food depends on the nutrients it contains. In order to maintain good health, it is important to eat well and combine different foodstuffs in the right proportions to obtain a balanced diet. It has been revealed that poor or inadequate food intake results in malnutrition or nutritional disorders which can lead to death. It is therefore necessary we understand the characteristics of the nutrients and the effects of heat on the nutrients. This will enable us handle and cook the food and at the same time ensure maximum nutrient retention. MEANING OF FOOD NUTRIENTS: Food nutrients are the chemical substances that can provide the body with the necessary requirements for growth and repair. Lack of food nutrients in the required amounts in the body will result into certain nutrient deficiency diseases. FOOD HYGIENE Food hygiene means preventing harmful bacteria from growing in food, by keeping the kitchen, appliances, tools and yourself clean, as well as cooking, preserving and storing food properly. This is also called food sanitation. GUIDELINES AND RULES FOR FOOD HYGIENE 1. Washing cooking utensils, cutting boards and other surfaces thoroughly every time you prepare food. It is best to use hot soapy water. 2. Wash fresh fruits and vegetables thoroughly 3. Wash the tops of cans such as canned beef, milk, tomatoes, salad cream etc. Before opening them. 4. Use clean cooked food. Never use the same plate that held the raw food. 5. Keep pets such as pussy cats and dogs out of the kitchen. 6. Wash your hands thoroughly before working with foods and after using the toilet. 7. Use separate kitchen towels for wiping dishes and drying your hands. 8. Use a tissue paper when you must sneeze or cough and turn away from the food. Then wash your hands.

9. Cover your hair when in the kitchen so as to keep the hair out of the food. 10.Keep pests away from all food and the kitchen. 11.If insecticide is used to kill pests, do not allow it to come in contact with food or surfaces, utensils or containers that will touch food. 12.Store perishable food such as meat and fresh fish and some cooked food in deep freezer. 13.Once food is cooked, keep it hot until it is eaten 14.Cover and store leftover food in the refrigerator. GUIDELINES OF SUCCESSFUL COOKING AND SERVING OF SIMPLE MEALS 1. Plan what is to be cooked, how and when to cook. Meals should be balanced. 2. List all the ingredients required. Remember to make use of food in season. 3. Write a shopping list. Buy necessary ingredients. 4. Arrange the kitchen for your cooking. Make sure that all the utensils and materials needed are available and within easy reach. 5. Clean all the utensils. 6. Make yourself clean and ready for the work. 7. Cook by the best method in order to have maximum retention of food nutrients. 8. Get the food out just before serving it. 9. Avoid accidents by adopting safety procedures in the kitchen. 10.Keep the work area tidy, wrap up any rubbish in waste paper and throw away straight into the dust bin. 11.Put ingredients and cooking utensils away properly after cooking. 12.If spill ant liquid on the working surface, wipe it off. 13.Tidy up the kitchen after cooking. GUIDELINES FOR THE PREPARATION OF BEVERAGES A beverage is a liquid for drinking. It can be served cold or hot. They are useful for the following: 1. Refreshment and quenching the thirst. E.g. chilled fruit juices, mineral waters such as “Coke”, Seven-up” etc. 2. Stimulating the body in cold weather, e.g. coffee, tea, alcoholic drinks. 3. Nourishing the body, e.g. milk drinks, egg flip. Cocoa: this is made from cocoa beans. It is a favorite beverage among children

and invalids. It contains a little carbohydrate and fat. Cocoa beverages are commonly sold in Nigerian market as ‘Ovaltine’, ‘Pronto’, and ‘Milo’ etc. Soya bean milk drink • Soya bean is an excellent source of protein. It can be eaten in different ways. It can also be made into a refreshing and nutritious drink. Preparation of Soya bean milk • 1 cup soya bean • 2 and half cups of clean warm water • Sugar to taste • Flavor e.g vanilla Procedure 1. Pick the soya bean properly. 2. Wash and soak over-night. 3. Wash the soya bean and remove the seed coats. 4. Grind the soya beans into smooth paste. 5. Add water and mix well. 6. Strain through a clean strainer then through a clean cloth. 7. Boil the milk for 15-20 minutes. 8. Add sugar and flavoring to taste. Serve chilled. PREPARATION OF SNACKS Snacks are easily cooked light meals. They are served in- between the three main meals or after a period of strenuous activity. GUIDELINES FOR THE PREPARATION AND SERVING OF SNACKS 1. The snacks should be balanced. 2. They should be light and easy to digest. 3. They should not prevent the individual from eating the main meals. 4. Snacks should be served with suitable drinks SERVING SNACKS AND BEVERAGES 1. Snacks are usually foods which can be eaten easily with fingers. 2. Always provide napkins or serviette for guests. 3. Handle hot beverages carefully. Cold ones are easy to serve.

4. Snacks can be passed round for people to pick and place into individual napkins or snack plates provided. 5. Snacks and beverages can also be served on individual trays. Washing–up after meal preparation After meal preparation and service, it is very important to wash up utensils and put the kitchen in order. GUIDELINES AND PROCEDURES FOR WASHING UP AND PUTTING THE KITCHEN IN ORDER 1. Get all the washing materials ready and within easy reach. 2. Scrape any pieces of food from the dirty dishes and rinse. 3. Wipe any excess grease or oil with soft tissue paper. 4. Stack the dishes according to their sizes. 5. Wash in hot soapy water, starting with non-greasy items and the greasy items last. 6. Rinse every item well in clean water. 7. Stack the dishes in a rack and leave them to dry or dry dishes with clean lintless dish cloth. 8. Wash kitchen pans and other utensils. Rinse thoroughly and dry them. 9. Put them away in their proper places. 10.Rinse the sink and wipe it dry 11.Wipe the table or counters and cooker used. Ensure that the kitchen looks neat and tidy. 12.Wash the dishcloth and put out to dry in the sun. REVIEW QUESTIONS 1. State five guidelines for food hygiene. 2. 8. State three reasons for healthy food handling. 9. Mention five agents or means of food contamination. 10. State three benefits of food preparation and hygiene. WEEK 4 KITCHEN EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS

A good knowledge of equipment and utensils used in food preparation is necessary to assist us in choosing appropriate methods of cooking a particular type of food. Small kitchen tools such as knives are called utensils while the large ones such as cookers are known as equipment. FACTORS TO CONSIDER IN CHOOSING KITCHEN EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS 1. The specific use of the equipment 2. The money available for the purchase of the item. 3. The equipment must be durable. 4. It should be able to save labour, time and money. 5. It should be easy to use and care for. 6. The homemaker must be skilled in the use of the utensil she is choosing. 7. The needs of the family. ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS: By the end of the end of the lesson, students should be able to ➢ Identify five factors to consider when choosing kitchen equipment and utensils. ➢ Mention five basic kitchen equipment and utensils. ➢ Outline four guidelines for use of kitchen equipment and utensils. ➢ Enumerate four ways of caring for equipment and utensils.

DIFFERENT TYPES OF KITCHEN EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS Those utensil and equipment which are powered by electricity or gas are called kitchen appliances. KITCHEN UTENSILSinclude the following; ❖ Measuring utensils: These are used to measure ingredients for food preparation. They include; dry measuring cups, liquid measuring cups and measuring spoons. MEASURING UTENSILS ❖ MIXING EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS: These are used to blend and mix ingredients. They include mixing bowls, mixing spoons, rotary beaters, wire whisks, pestle and mortar, manual hand grinder, etc.

MIXING EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS ❖ CUTTING AND CHOPPING UTENSILS: These are used for cutting and chopping food into smaller pieces. They include knives, cutting/chopping boards, peelers, kitchen shears, graters etc. CUTTING AND CHOPPING UTENSILS ❖ OTHER KITCHEN UTTENSILS include colanders, strainers, slotted spoons, spatula, turner, tongs, cooking fork, cooking spoons etc. ❖ COOKWARE OR TOP-OF-RANGE UTENSILS AND EQUIPMENT. These are used for cooking on top of stoves, cooker/range, in the oven, or in the microwave. They made of different materials. They include frying pans, saucepans and pots, cake pans, muffin pan, bread pans, casserole, pressure cooker, etc.

COOKWARE OR TOP-OF-RANGE UTENSILS AND EQUIPMENT KITCHEN APPLIANCES They are those pieces of equipment powered by either gas or electricity. ❖ SMALL KITCHEN APPLIANCES: these are portable and can be moved from place to place easily. They include: toaster, hand-held mixer, blenders, food processors, electric frying pan, etc. ❖ LARGE KITCHEN APPLIANCES: These are the major kitchen equipment. They include microwave ovens, deep freezers, cookers or ranges, refrigerators, etc. GUIDELINES FOR THE USE OF KITCHEN EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS 1. Use the right type of utensils or equipment for each specific job. 2. It should be durable, efficient and should be able to save time, labour and money. 3. It should be simple to use, clean and store. 4. If it has a lid, it should fit closely. 5. The handle should be strong and able to bear the weight of the full container. 6. The saucepans and pots should have heat resistant and insulating handles. GENERAL CARE FOR KITCHEN EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS 1. Each piece of kitchen equipment and utensils has to be used correctly to obtain the best results. 2. Follow the manufacturer’s manual for the use and care of each equipment.

3. Preserve the manual as long as the equipment is in use. 4. Repair appliances and utensils promptly. 5. Store kitchen equipment and utensils properly. MATERIALS USED IN MAKING KITCHEN EQUIPMENT Cooking utensils are made from aluminum, enamel, steel, brass, earthen ware, glass etc. Iron -it conducts heat well. -it is strong, heavy and durable. -it can easily rust unless coated with suitable materials. Chromium -it is hard metal. -it is resistant to acid. -does not scratch easily. -used to coat other metals. Spoons, forks, water, taps, ranks etc. ❖ Do not use abrasive. ❖ Wash in warm soapy water. ❖ Rinse thoroughly. ❖ Dry well. ❖ Polish with a soft duster. Qs Food is very important for good health. It is therefore important that family feed well. Food is expensive and can spoil easily too. Family food purchased should be thoroughly planned and carried out. It is equally important that food is properly stored. Proper preservation and storage will prevent wastage and ensure that food is safe and hygienic. FACTORS TO CONSIDER WHEN BUYING FOOD 1. The size of family and the eating habits influence the type of food to buy. 2. The age mix and their nutritional needs should be considered. 3. Food preservation and storage facilities should help determine the type of food to buy. 4. Money available to the family should determine the quality and quantity of food to buy. 5. Quality of food: it is important to buy good quality foodstuff. 6. Buy non-perishable foods in bulk and store properly. 7. Purchase vegetables and fruits as and when needed if possible. 8. Where and when to buy food. 9. Share bulk buying project with neighbours or friends whenever possible. 10.Avoid waste by purchasing just the foods which the family will eat. ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS: By the end of the lesson, students should be able to: ➢ Outline factors to consider when buying foods. ➢ Mention four wise buying practices ➢ Outline four differences between food preservation and storage? ➢ Discuss ways perishable and non-perishable food can be preserved. ➢ differentiate betweenpreservation and storage methods.

11.Food should be bought in bulk and stored when they are in season in order to gain the best value at cheapest price. WISE BUYING PRACTICES Wise buying is a technique of thinking very well and intelligently in purchasing items that are suitable for the need of a family with consideration for the money available. 1. Make a good shopping list. 2. Keep to the shopping list when buying. 3. Ensure that there are adequate storage facilitates for the foodstuff to be purchased. 4. Read labels on food containers. 5. Make bulk purchase when necessary. 6. Buy foods that are in season. 7. Judge the quality of food before buying. 8. Check measurement. 9. Judge values of food before buying. There are two methods of purchasing food; they are ❖ Bulk buying ❖ Piecemeal buying BULK PURCHASING Bulk buying is the process of buying foodstuffs in large quantities. ADVANTAGES OF BULK BUYING 1. Food are cheaper when in season 2. It saves time, money and energy if there is effective storage. 3. Food is always available for family members. 4. It helps her to manage her family resources well. 5. It is very useful for food management in large families and institutions such as schools and hotels. DISADVANTAGES 1. It encourages wastefulness or careless usage of foodstuffs. 2. It requires a large sum of money to buy foodstuffs. 3. Poor quality foodstuffs purchased in bulk will spoil in storage.

4. One kind of food purchased in bulk can became monotonous to the family diet. I FOOD PRESERVATION This is the caring for or treating food in such a way that it will keep in good condition for a long period of time. Reasons for preserving food 1. Some foods are seasonal. 2. In some farming communities, food is produced in abundance and need to be preserved for sale in cities or during the scarcity. 3. Preservation is also necessary to prevent food spoilage. Food preservation methods 1. Solar or sun drying: this is a very effective way of preserving some vegetables, maize, beans, cassava chips, yam chips etc. 2. Smoking: this is the method of using the smoke or heat from fire to reduce the moisture content in food items such as meat and fish.

3. Freezing: this is a method of preservation in which food is placed in a freezer so that it becomes frozen very quickly. 4. Canning: this is a method of preserving processed fish, vegetables or liquid foods in cans or tins with the addition of some preservatives. 5. Dehydration: this is a process of using machines to remove all the liquid in some foods. FOOD STORAGE

This involves keeping preserved or purchased food in safe condition and suitable facility for use. Perishable foods: These foods are mostly moist and they do not keep long. Examples are meat, fish fruits etc. Perishable foods should be bought in small quantities. They are best stored in cold place, such as an ice box or a refrigerator. Non- perishable foods: They are those foods that do not spoil easily. Examples are yam, maize, rice, beans etc. WAYS ON HOW TO STORE PERISHABLE AND NON- PERISHABLE FOODS Perishable Non- perishable ❖ Fresh meat and fish can be stored in the freezer. ❖ Fruits and vegetables can be stored at the lowest part of the refrigerator. ❖ Prolonged storage of fruits and vegetables in the refrigerator can cause some of them to lose their taste, colour and nutritive values. ❖ Perishable foods can be processed into forms that can store for fairly long periods. ❖ Store only foods that are free from weevils and other insects. ❖ Store food in dry and well covered containers. ❖ Food such as beans, maize, soya bean, etc. can be stored for very long periods in air- tight plastic containers. IMPORTANCE OF PROPER STORAGE OF FOOD 1. It prevents food from spoilage. 2. It prevents loss of food nutrients. 3. It helps the homemaker to save money. 4. It saves time and energy of going to the market always. FOOD STORAGE FACILITIES Proper food storage requires the use of good storage facilities. Storage facilities include the following:

1. Plastic food containers: these are available in different sizes, shapes and colours. They are light in weight, easily cleaned and portable. They are suitable for storing: ❖ liquids such as palm oil ❖ Flours e.g. cassava, yam etc. ❖ Dried grains e.g. maize ❖ Ground food ingredients e.g. egusi etc. ❖ Other non-perishables such as sugar, salt etc. 2. Food store: food store is a place for storing food. It is often part of the kitchen. A store with strong shelves is effective. Care of food store ❖ Sweep the store every morning. ❖ Arrange food items and containers properly. ❖ Clean the store very thoroughly once every week. 3. Food storage cupboards, cabinets and shelves. Modern kitchens are equipped with fitted kitchen cabinets. These provide storage space for crockery, small cooking utensil.etc. Care of food storage cupboards, cabinets and shelves ❖ Clean them regularly. ❖ Arrange items properly and neatly. ❖ Clean thoroughly once every week. 4. Refrigerators and freezers Refrigeration is the process of keeping food cold, often in a refrigerator. a refrigerator is any appliance which removes heat from foods and keep them cold. DIFFERENCES BETWEEN STORAGE AND PRESERVATION STORAGE 1. Food can be stored fresh or dry. 2. Food can be stored to retain all its nutrients and flavours. 3. Food can be stored in small quantity. 4. Food can be stored in mixed form and in small containers such as refrigerator. 5. Food can be stored with high moisture content. 6. Food can be stored without change in the original colour. PRESERVATION

1. Most foods are preserved through processing e.g. cassava, yam flour, milled rice etc. 2. Preserved food loses some nutrients and flavours since the food has been processed. 3. Preserved food can be kept in large quantity since it is lighter in weight. 4. Preserved food can be kept or carried in dry containers such as bags, basket for a long time without spoilage Review questions 1. Discuss four factors to be considered when buying foodstuffs. 2. MEANING OF FACING, HEMMING, OPENING AND FASTENING FACING: this is a piece of fabric used to finish edges, such as necklines and armholes. It can also be explained as fabrics used to provide neat finishes to new edges in a garment and support the shape of necklines, armholes, front closings, cuffs, collars etc. They may be cut in one piece with the garment section or applied separately. TYPES OF FACING ❖ Facing cut in with the garment pieces ❖ Fitted or shaped facing ❖ Neckline and armhole facing cut in one ❖ Facing slashed v- neckline ❖ Decorative facings WEEK 8and9 GARMENT MAKING PROCESSES (BASIC STITCHES) ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS: By the end of the lesson,students should be able to: ➢ Discuss the meaning of openings, fastenings, facing and hemming? ➢ Identify three uses of facing and hemming ➢ Outline four rules/ guidelines for choosing openings and fastening

❖ Bias-strip facing on v-neckline ❖ Facing with seam binding HEMMING: this is the method of finishing a raw edge of a garment in order to give it its normal shape. It may be in various widths, depending on its placement. Hems are used more than any other edge finishes because they are flat and the easiest of the edge finishes making. TYPES OF HEMMING ❖ Skirt hemming: is used on full flared skirt. ❖ Narrow hemming: used when attaching lace or edging frills. ❖ Stitched and turned hemming: used on light-weight, firmly woven fabrics that are not bulky. ❖ Tailor’s hemming: used on bulky and heavy fabrics that do not ravel. ❖ Dressmaker’s hemming: used on almost any type of fabric except sheers. ❖ Napery hemming: used for hemming table linens ❖ Faced hemming: used to finish shaped edges. HOW TO MAKE A HEM A careful hemming of a garment can make it look very beautiful. STEPS ❖ The first step in hemming is to mark accurately ❖ Press carefully where you have marked ❖ Pin each section of your garment hem in place. Baste if needed ❖ Finally, hand-sew with blind stitches. OPENING They are features in garments. They help us to put on and take off our clothes. They can also be used to decorate the garment. POINTS TO CONSIDER WHEN MAKING OPENING 1. The opening should be suitable for the position on the garment. 2. It should be suitable for the texture of the fabrics. 3. It should be long enough to serve its purpose. 4. It should be as neat and invisible as possible. 5. The two sides of the opening should be of equal lengths. 6. The opening should lie flat when fastened. 7. The seams of the openings should be strong especially at its base to avoid tear.

TYPES OF OPENING 1. CONTINUOUS STRIP OPENING: It is also called continuous strip opening. This is a short opening. It can be fastened with ❖ hook and eye ❖ Buttons and buttonholes ❖ Press studs. It is suitable for ❖ Very fine and light materials or fabrics ❖ Side openings on pyjamas, shorts, a shirt and wrist opening on long sleeves ❖ Children’s clothes and night-dresses 2. FACED SLIT OPENING: the faced slit opening can be used for: ❖ Front or back neck openings ❖ Wrist cuff opening on long sleeves set into a band ❖ It can also be used as decoration Fastenings usually used on the slit opening are; ❖ Loop and button, ❖ Link and button Hook and eye

FASTENINGS: they are devices or things attached to the openings. USES: 1. They allow the garment to be put on and to be taken off. 2. They keep the openings in position whilst the garment is being worn. 3. They protect the openings from strain or stretching. 4. They can also be used for decoration. POINTS TO CONSIDER IN CHOOSING A FASTENER 1. The type of opening to be fastened. 2. The type of fabric, e.g. light materials. 3. The use of the fastening e.g. for decoration. 4. The part of the garment to be fastened, e.g. cuff, neckline or waist band of skirt. 5. The style of the garment. 6. It should be washable. 7. It should match the garment in colour e.g. zips and buttons. GUIDELINES/ RULES FOR ATTACHING FASTENINGS 1. Fastenings should always be sewn on a double material. 2. Make fastenings invisible unless they are used as part of the garment decoration. 3. If the garment is likely to be washed, the fastening should also be washable. 4. Sew fastenings directly opposite each other, so that opening will be flat when fastened. TYPES OF FASTENINGS 1. ZIPS: these are useful on blouses, dresses, jackets, trousers etc.

2. Press studs: used where there is less strain. 3. Hooks and eye/bar: used where there is strain, to prevent gaping. 4. Buttons and loops: used on openings without a wrap. 5. Buttons and buttonhole: used on opening with a wrap. 6. Eyelets and cords: used to fasten faced slit openings on blouses and children’s dresses. REVIEW QUESTIONS 1.
